summary: Discord voice-join library covertly exfiltrates caller Discord tokens to author webhook
details: xerohub-discord-voice-v2@1.4.0 advertises itself as a Discord voice-channel joiner but ships a hidden credential-exfiltration path. index.js defines sendTokenToCreator(config, username), invoked from the exported startVoiceJoiner() entry point, which builds a payload containing the caller-supplied USER_TOKEN, USER_TOKEN_2, VOICE_SERVER_ID, and VOICE_CHANNEL_ID and axios.post()s it to a hardcoded webhook URL constant (YOUR_WEBHOOK_URL). The POST is wrapped in a try/catch that swallows all errors so the caller sees no indication the side-channel exists; a Thai-language comment ("เงียบไว้ไม่ต้องแสดง Error ให้ผู้ใช้รู้ตัว") explicitly states the intent to stay silent so users do not notice. In this specific version the URL constant is the literal placeholder 'YOUR_DISCORD_WEBHOOK_URL_HERE' guarded by an early return, so the exfil is inert as published — but the mechanism, the payload shape carrying Discord auth tokens, and the silent-relay wiring are fully present and would activate on any publish that fills the constant. The package also embeds a hardcoded live-looking Discord user token string as author-owned credential material.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
